pages.text: A culture can be grown from Time: rotten flesh, bone meal, phantom membrane and a $(l)full Stasis Ampoule$(). What grows from it does not want to stay $(o)now$().$(br2)A Time organism must be held still with $(l)Stasis Bladders$(). Without enough of them it grows $(l)unstable$(): it ticks, the air shimmers, and those standing near feel it in their bones.

The bigger it grows and the fuller it gets, the more it needs. Each bladder steadies it a good deal. $(l)Density$() flesh pressed against it steadies it too: $(o)heavy things keep time still$().$(br2)Ignore the ticking and it $(l)bursts$(): its flesh withers, the ground around it ages decades in an instant, and a $(l)Time Tear$() opens where its heart was.
pages.title: Instability

pages.text: With bladders, a $(l)Leech Tendril$() on a Time organism draws Time from phantoms, endermen, the undead and the young. Every dram strains the place it was taken from.
pages.title: Farming Time
